intent.title: [config-source-authorization/1] Contain filesystem config operations
intent.responsibility: Hydra core implementer: enforce per-source native containment in file load, lookup and listing, with immediate 1.4 migration guidance.
acceptance: AC17-AC19: in-root files and links work; traversal, same-prefix siblings and external links fail before read/list in load/group/config/list paths.
AC18: native Windows drive/UNC/junction cases pass on Windows; all-skipped native coverage is not a Windows verification result.
AC20: document the stable-filesystem limit, immediate 1.4 break and separate-source migration; numeric news fragment is required before publication.

display.summary: Keep filesystem config access inside its source root.

intent.title: [config-source-authorization/2] Contain package config resources
intent.responsibility: Hydra core implementer: reuse the native guard and add rooted package/archive resource traversal without extraction or losing supported regular-package loading.
acceptance: AC17-AC19: package load/lookup/list cannot reach sibling packages or archive subtrees; internal links still work and external links fail.
Existing source, compiled-initializer, zip and namespace-parent fixtures pass; exercise a rooted ResourceReader without coercing it to Path.
Unestablished roots fail before read/list; compatibility and later source-unsafe operation cannot disable containment.

display.summary: Keep package and archive config access inside its source root.

intent.title: [config-source-authorization/3] Restore scoped plugin registries
intent.responsibility: Hydra core implementer: remove eager external discovery from registry construction and restore Hydra-owned plugin/source-type state across initialization and failure.
acceptance: AC21-AC22: explicit register imports no unrelated plugin; discover/get_stats/instantiate preserve compatibility discovery when actually requested.
Normal exit, constructor failure, exceptions, clear-then-exit and refused nested initialization restore prior presence/maps and application registrations.
Previously scoped custom source implementations do not remain usable after restoration; Python import effects are not claimed undone.

display.summary: Restore plugin registries when initialization ends or fails.

intent.title: [config-source-authorization/4] Warn loaded namespace plugin authors
intent.responsibility: Hydra core implementer: warn for successful namespace-only discovery using actual entry-point coverage and align the plugin-author migration guide.
acceptance: AC14: a loaded legacy class emits a visible identified warning and migration URL; an equivalent working entry point suppresses that warning.
Invalid/failed entry points and unenumerable-editable warnings do not count as migration success.
AC15: the guide covers concrete-class packaging, registration imports, reinstall and --info plugins; a numeric publication fragment is required.

display.summary: Warn namespace-plugin authors and guide entry-point migration.

intent.title: [config-source-authorization/5] Unify effective authorization state
intent.responsibility: Hydra core implementer: unify immutable per-category policy, replacement, release defaults and config-load guard state while preserving execution adapters and non-whitelistable authorization controls.
acceptance: AC10-AC13: ordinary lists add, replace changes one category, [] differs from replace([]), explicit lists enable checks under LEGACY, unsafe inheritance/replacement and context restoration follow the accepted rules.

Existing execution calls/context reset remain equivalent for the release; omitted values inherit, 1.5 defaults are empty and explicit LEGACY is rejected. Reused/overlapping policies do not leak mutable overlays or tokens.

Authorization construction/context/helpers and canonical aliases are non-whitelistable instantiate targets even with exact grants. The config-load guard rejects grant-making API entry but passive checks and normal trusted Python use remain supported.

display.summary: Share authorization state while preserving execution APIs.

intent.title: [config-source-authorization/6] Select plugins before imports
intent.responsibility: Hydra core implementer: resolve entry-point names or explicit class selectors from metadata, gate imports and cached visibility, and enforce scoped registration and namespace settings.
acceptance: AC21: denied initializers stay untouched; entry-point names, explicit classes and exported aliases work. Unknown or ambiguous names fail before import; identical metadata identities deduplicate.
AC24: disabled scanning makes no scan imports; authorized entry points may remain under hydra_plugins. Explicit scan=True with checked plugin grants fails before discovery.

Cached class/scheme presence and later Compose grants do not widen initialized discovery. Config-load-time register cannot grant; scoped trusted application registration remains usable and restores correctly.

display.summary: Select authorized plugins before importing them.

intent.title: [config-source-authorization/7] Gate config sources before initialization
intent.responsibility: Hydra core implementer: enforce source identity, private declaration provenance and config-load/conversion guards at repository, override and ConfigStore boundaries.
acceptance: AC3-AC7: deny undeclared file/pkg/named structured/custom requests before implementation resolution, construction, availability or imports. Source/data conversion cannot expand grants; normal ConfigStore registration works.

AC4/AC6/AC16: literal CLI/Compose selections and trusted initialization/hooks authorize once; config aliases/interpolations, provider strings, changed markers and saved rerun values cannot forge that provenance.

AC19: inspection/completion/sweep and per-call caches preserve checks and scopes; custom schemes also need implementation permission. Guard restoration handles nested conversion and failure without suppressing normal authorized target execution.

display.summary: Check config sources and stop config loading from granting permissions.

intent.title: [config-source-authorization/8] Install worker policy before restore
intent.responsibility: Hydra core and launcher implementer: transport trusted policy and registry declarations before worker discovery/composition, restore reused workers and document external launcher participation.
acceptance: AC23: Basic, Joblib process backends and Submitit receiving paths establish policy before singleton/discovery/source/sweep/logging operations, including resubmission and resolved plugin identities.

Reused workers and failures restore prior permissions/visibility. Job config cannot broaden transported grants, forge origin markers or enable namespace scanning; no live ContextVar token is serialized.
Missing/inconsistent bootstrap and unsupported launchers fail before dispatch whenever any required category is checked; only all-LEGACY 1.4 may warn and use the old contract.

display.summary: Give workers the policy before they restore Hydra state.

intent.title: [config-source-authorization/9] Expose and document the integrated policy
intent.responsibility: Hydra core implementer: expose the approved module API, main/initialize source list, initializer deprecation, CLI plugin lists and scoped unsafe options, then document and verify the integrated journeys.
acceptance: AC1-AC2/AC6/AC25: main/initialize declare primary plus ordered additional sources and authorize once; caller-relative and global/context adapter behavior is preserved with a deprecation warning.

Public AuthorizationPolicy/replace/LEGACY exports match the approved module API. Same-call explicit policy plus old execution argument fails before side effects; local adapters remain valid. Plugin CLI accepts entry names, comma lists and repeated flags.

AC4/AC8-AC13: literal Compose/CLI source overrides authorize only the call; config-derived requests do not. Unsafe source use is scoped, 1.4 warnings and 1.5 defaults/rejection match policy, and the next checked call refuses ungranted sources.

AC9/AC20: category grants and source-unsafe options do not permit logging/instantiate policy controls or disable containment. Run representative integrated journeys and current validation; exact numeric news paths and refreshed review are delivery prerequisites.

display.summary: Expose and document the integrated Python and CLI APIs.
